correctness.rationale: PASS: Prime steps strictly add k and every composite step maps to a prime; no fixed points, no adjacent composite states, and every cycle contains a composite. Period two has (p,pm) with k=p(m−1) and P⁺(m)≤p; period three has one composite and p,p+k,p+2k, forces p|2k and p=2 by the primality obstruction, so k=2^a−1 with 2^a+1 prime (Fermat exponent). Period four has two composites alternating or one composite after three primes. The former gives distinct p,q, CRT k=tpq−p−q and necessary/sufficient two smooth multipliers; latter forces p=3, k=3^u−1, primality of 3^u+2 and 2·3^u+1. Each converse proves least period four. Independent bounded trajectory calculations confirmed observed short cycles for tested k; they do not establish global completeness.
